# Decision history — evidence-intake-project

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## evidence-intake-project.decision.adapters-may-propose-structural-edges

### Revision 1 — A NormalizedBatch may carry suggested structural edges (temporally_overlaps, derived_from, refers_to) between nodes the case already holds

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.adapters-may-propose-structural-edges/1` · scope `path "adapters/**"`, `path "docs/normalized-input.md"`, `path "src/ingest.rs"`, `path "src/store.rs"`

The ingest contract gains `NormalizedBatch.edges: Vec<NormalizedEdge>` (serde default empty, so every existing batch document still parses). A NormalizedEdge names two endpoints by (NodeKind, id) restricted to Source and Content, a relation restricted to the structural kinds `temporally_overlaps`, `derived_from` and `refers_to`, a required written rationale, and an ExtractionProvenance that must be machine_generated with review_state `suggested`. `import_normalized` inserts them after the batch's own sources and content, in the same transaction, with `created_by = "suggest:<extractor>@<version>"` -- the same prefix the analyzers use, because that prefix is how `review_queue` recognises a machine-proposed edge and an adapter's proposal is exactly that. Import refuses: an endpoint that does not exist in the case (checked with the same node lookup `link_evidence` uses, after the batch's own rows are inserted, so a batch may relate the sources it brings), an endpoint in another case, any relation outside the three, any non-suggested or human-attributed provenance, an empty rationale, and an edge already held between the same pair in either direction with the same relation. A batch may contain edges and no sources at all: that is how a later pass relates two originals imported on different days.

**Context.** The cross-camera audio sync slice needs to state one fact about two originals -- camera B's soundtrack lags camera A's by so many milliseconds -- and the kernel had no place for it: `import_normalized` refuses an already-imported source id or hash, and NormalizedBatch carried only sources, segments and content. An observation on one source's segment naming the other in prose would be lossy and one-sided; the kernel already has the vocabulary (`EdgeKind::TemporallyOverlaps`, `NodeKind::Source`) and the machine-edge convention (`suggest:` created_by, direction-blind duplicate check) from the analyzers. Restricting adapters to structural relations keeps the evaluative ones (supports, contradicts, corroborates, impeaches ...) with the analyzers and with people: an adapter measures how records sit relative to each other; it never says what they establish. Derived stills also finally get an honest `derived_from` edge to their original instead of a prose note.

**Consequences.** docs/normalized-input.md documents the edge shape. The video adapter's soundtrack, still, and sync mappers can emit edges; the first users are `derived_from` (still -> original video, statement content -> soundtrack) and `temporally_overlaps` (source A -> source B with the measured offset and correlation peak in the rationale). The numeric offset lives in the rationale text with a stable leading form (`audio cross-correlation: <B> lags <A> by <n> ms (peak <p>)`) rather than a new column: normalising two device clocks onto one axis remains a hypothesis a person writes as a time_basis, so the kernel needs the measurement to be reviewable, not computable. Whether a later pass may also append new segments to an already-imported identical original is a separate open question (@evidence-intake-project.ingest.append-to-identical-source-question).

## evidence-intake-project.decision.akr-ledger-is-published

### Revision 1 — The AKR ledger is published with the source

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.akr-ledger-is-published/1` · scope `path ".akr/**"`, `path ".gitignore"`, `path "docs/generated/**"`, `path "sources/**"`

The .akr ledger, its generated views, and registered sources are part of the published repository. They are not private files. Gitignore covers working artifacts only: build output, local databases, model weights, vendored research checkouts, agent-pack binaries, agent scratch, and personal media such as Damion_1-2.jpg. .akr/cache stays ignored because it is rebuildable.

**Context.** A public export to github.com/liminalism/EvidenceIntake omitted .akr on the assumption it was private. The owner corrected that. Extraneous development artifacts should be gitignored so a normal push is clean.

**Consequences.** origin is github.com/liminalism/EvidenceIntake. A clone of the public repository receives the ledger. Cache, SQLite files, model packs, and local samples do not.

## evidence-intake-project.decision.analyzer-classes-are-disjoint

### Revision 1 — An analyzer proposes relationships, proposes interpretations, or reports findings — three disjoint classes

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.analyzer-classes-are-disjoint/1` · scope `path "src/store.rs"`, `path "src/store/enrichment_rules.rs"`, `path "src/suggest.rs"`

SuggestionKind classifies every analyzer into exactly one of three classes, and the predicates are exhaustive and disjoint. proposes_relationships writes suggested edges. proposes_interpretations writes suggested rows in content_interpretations -- a reading of one passage, which has no second endpoint to point at. reports_findings derives gaps on every run and stores nothing. reports_findings is defined as neither of the other two, so a new analyzer joins a class by construction rather than by being remembered in every walk over SuggestionKind::ALL.

**Context.** The interpretation layer added eleven analyzers to the eight the case already had. Eight of them propose readings rather than edges, and the existing rule was a single boolean: an analyzer either proposed relationships or reported findings. Store::suggest was taught the new class with an inline match, but Store::open_gaps -- which case_standing calls -- still asked every analyzer that did not propose relationships for its findings, and Store::findings answers that with InvalidAuthoring. Every test in tests/standing.rs failed on `inherit-profile proposes relationships and reports no findings`, an error message that describes neither what happened nor what is true.

**Consequences.** Adding an analyzer means adding it to one predicate. Anything walking SuggestionKind::ALL asks reports_findings first rather than negating a different question. The domain rule the classes encode is unchanged: an analyzer either proposes something a person must answer, or reports work nobody has done, and never both.

## evidence-intake-project.decision.audio-adapter-native-whisper-engine

### Revision 1 — The audio adapter transcribes in process with a feature-gated fork of franken_whisper, not whisper-rs

`superseded` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.audio-adapter-native-whisper-engine/1` · scope `path "adapters/audio/**"`

The `--model-path` backend of `evidence-audio` is `NativeWhisperBackend` (adapters/audio/src/native.rs), built on the pure-Rust native engine of franken_whisper (github.com/Dicklesworthstone/franken_whisper). It replaces the whisper-rs/whisper.cpp backend, which is removed. The crate is consumed with `default-features = false` from a local fork -- sibling checkout `../franken_whisper`, branch `evidence-intake`, `upstream` remote pointing at the original -- whose only change is a `full` feature (default-on upstream) that gates the CLI, orchestrator, bridge backends, diarization, storage, sync, robot and YouTube modules, plus a `distribution` feature for the model downloader. The engine reads the same ggml/gguf files whisper.cpp reads; the adapter never resolves or downloads a model. Statements are stamped `franken_whisper@<model>/<crate version>`. The `native-whisper` feature is on by default because the build is pure Rust (no cmake, no C++ toolchain).

**Context.** Unforked, franken_whisper pulls 353 crates including a TLS stack, a second pure-Rust SQLite, and an async runtime -- none of it reachable from the engine, none of it optional. The engine itself (src/native_engine) depends only on ft-core, ft-kernel-cpu, half, rayon, serde, sha2 and thiserror, about thirty crates. Gating the rest raised the adapter's dependency count from 90 to 118 rather than to 350. The upstream license is MIT with a rider withholding rights from named AI companies; the owner judged that rider not to bear on this project's use of it, and intends to move the project off AGPL. Measured on jfk.wav (11 s) with tiny.en on a plain `nightly` build without target-cpu flags: 0.54 s wall.

**Consequences.** The engine's decode parameters can be overridden by `FW_*` environment variables (FW_BEAM_SIZE, FW_INITIAL_PROMPT, FW_TEMP_BEST_OF, FW_RETRY_FAILED_WINDOW, ...) which the stamped version string does not record; an operator's environment could change decoding silently. Word timings from the engine carry no per-word probability, so statement confidence is the segment's exp(mean token logprob) carried through `avg_logprob`. The upstream measures its speed advantage with `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3`; without that flag in this workspace's cargo config the kernels run on the SSE2 baseline. The path dependency assumes the sibling checkout exists; a git dependency on a pushed fork would make clean clones build. Syncing upstream means merging into `evidence-intake` and re-checking `cargo check --no-default-features` in the fork.

**superseded by** `@evidence-intake-project.decision.single-broker-inference/1`

## evidence-intake-project.decision.keyframe-finder-is-an-index

### Revision 1 — Keyframe embeddings are a case-local finder index: hidden candidate selection, chronological display, never a score or evidence

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.keyframe-finder-is-an-index/1` · scope `all`

Keyframe retrieval is a finder index, not evidence. Each coverage- or scene-selected derived still is embedded once by an EmbeddingBackend (JSON for tests, a load-once local CLI for overnight SigLIP-class runs) and stored against that still's source id. A later query is embedded by the same pinned model and preprocessing. The kernel compares the query to every vector in the case, selects at most the reviewer's requested limit by descending internal cosine similarity with source id as the deterministic tie-breaker, discards the similarity numbers, and reorders the selected locators by still identifier for chronological presentation. A hit names the original hash, time range on that original, and derived still. Similarity is never stored on a hit, printed, or exported. There is no model-independent fixed cosine cut: the synthetic 0.20 cut returned zero candidates in the first live SigLIP 2 run. A future stopping rule requires human-labeled, pinned-model evidence and still may not expose a number or bias selection toward the start of a recording.

Vectors live as a little-endian f32 BLOB on a STRICT keyframe_embeddings table keyed (source_id, model), with case_id and a same-case trigger. Comparison is brute-force cosine. sqlite-vec is not loaded: a case holds hundreds to low tens of thousands of sampled vectors, not millions; an extension would make in-memory tests and the Windows GUI depend on load_extension; and export exclusion is structural only if export_case never queries the table. Replacing the scan with sqlite-vec later is an implementation change behind the same read model, not a new contract.

Embeddings are not a NormalizedBatch field and not content. Indexing writes no observation and no edge; a reviewer who wants a claim about a frame authors it. A later overnight pass indexes stills the case already holds, which avoids the open question of appending segments to an identical source. Import refuses a vector that is empty, non-finite, zero-norm, or whose dimension disagrees with others of the same model in the case, and refuses a source that is not a derived still (derived_from another source in the same case). Re-running the same (source_id, model) replaces the vector. Cases never share vectors. Every export audience skips the table.

**Context.** The work record asked for CLIP/SigLIP-class embeddings behind a VisionBackend-style trait, a SearchHit-style locator, no similarity number, recall over precision, no observation or edge from retrieval, and storage in SQLite as either a blob column or sqlite-vec. The kernel already has FTS5 for words; this is the visual analogue, and structure-not-verdict already allows ranking matches so long as the number is withheld. Scene-core already emits derived stills with a derived_from edge, so the original hash and timeline locator are joinable without the adapter asserting what the frame shows.

**Consequences.** Store::index_keyframes / Store::search_keyframes and the KeyframeHit read model are the kernel contract. The video adapter gains EmbeddingBackend, JSON and CLI backends, and embed_keyframes. The kernel CLI gains index-frames and find-frames; the video CLI gains embed and find. The cosine cut is KEYFRAME_SIMILARITY_CUT (0.20), settled on synthetic unit vectors — real CLIP/SigLIP scores against discovery footage were not measured. A live encoder is optional overnight; tests never call one.

**Retired claims** — `#cut-then-identifier`, dropped at this revision.

## evidence-intake-project.decision.not-a-case-management-system

### Revision 1 — The product is discovery collation, not a CMS, DEMS or time tracker; platform interop is at the export-folder level

`superseded` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.not-a-case-management-system/1` · scope `all`

The software reads a discovery production and produces the discovery review a defender otherwise writes by hand -- what the state has for each element, what contradicts, what is missing, what to raise, what to ask the client -- through the existing read models (Overview, CaseStanding, DecisionBrief, exports). It does not become a case-management system: no calendar, scheduling, notes-as-CMS, SMS, timekeeping, reporting for funders, client demographics, conflict checks, or document assembly. It does not become a digital evidence management system that hosts, streams, redacts or shares productions. Interoperability with the platforms discovery arrives on (Axon Evidence exports, prosecutor portals, USB dumps) is at the file level: ingest the exported folder -- media plus its metadata and audit CSV -- into a production; never integrate with the platform, log in to it, or hold credentials for it.

**Context.** Practitioner threads in r/publicdefenders describe DefenderData, Clio, MyCase and LegalServer; every complaint is CMS UX (calendar, notes placement, mobile, reports, tabs) and every positive use is administrative (dockets by date, assignments, storing Axon links). None of it is analysis of the record. Meanwhile the artifact defenders build from a discovery packet by hand -- a Word memo of charges, exposure, brief facts, witnesses, bond, criminal history and open issues, written "so anyone can pick up my file" -- is exactly the read models this kernel already produces. Building CMS features would compete with entrenched, cheap, funder-mandated tools on their turf; the collation kernel is the part nobody serves.

**Consequences.** Feature requests that are really CMS or DEMS requests are declined and pointed at the office's existing system; the export read models are the integration surface for anyone who wants collation output inside a CMS. An Axon export-folder ingest is a legitimate adapter and can be planned; an Axon API client is not. Case isolation and the docket view stay minimal: enough to open, list and separate cases, not to manage them.

**superseded by** `@evidence-intake-project.decision.office-layer-around-the-kernel/1`

## evidence-intake-project.decision.office-layer-around-the-kernel

### Revision 1 — The product becomes a PD case system: an office layer wraps the evidence kernel, which itself stays collation-only

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.office-layer-around-the-kernel/1` · scope `all`

The product expands from an evidence-collation utility to an open-source public-defender case system: DefenderData rebuilt around the evidence itself. The expansion happens beside the kernel, never inside it. The evidence kernel (evidence_intake: sources, content, entities, propositions, events, charges, review, suggest, export) keeps every existing boundary: no calendar, office notes, tasks, messaging, demographics, timekeeping or reporting enters its schema; evidentiary events never become court-calendar events; advocacy items never become office tasks; entities stay case-scoped; machines still confer nothing. Case management is a sibling domain — an office-core workspace crate with its own store and database — holding users, clients (one person across many matters, with aliases and contacts), matters, assignments, courts, appearances and deadlines, custody and offer state, office notes with immutable authorship, tasks, and later reporting, custom fields and flags. A matter carries an optional evidence_case_id reference into the kernel; neither schema depends semantically on the other, and the boundary is enforced in the application layer. A client-to-evidence-entity identity link is made by a named person from a possible-match prompt, never inferred from a name. Privileged kernel material (advocacy items, annotations, decision briefs) is never readable from the office database or any office view or export. Platform interoperability stays at the exported-folder file level: the software never authenticates to Axon, a prosecutor portal, or any discovery platform. Still out of scope: billing and invoicing, trust accounting, payment processing, e-filing, legal research, video conferencing, generic CRM, platform API integration, and AI drafting.

**Context.** The 2026-08-30 outside review (source defenderdata-cms-expansion-review-2026-08-30) examined DefenderData marketing and r/publicdefenders practitioner usage and concluded the project already holds the hardest 25-35% of a DefenderData replacement — provenance, multimodal intake, review semantics, charge-element analysis — while the missing surface is broad but shallower: clients, matters, calendar, notes, office search, reporting, multi-user. The owner adopted the expansion on 2026-08-30 and chose a calendar-first presentation with the GUI split into a Court pane (daily schedule and responsibilities) and an Office pane (case and evidence intake, paralegal and PD review). This supersedes decision.not-a-case-management-system, whose kernel-protecting rationale survives here as the inner boundary rather than the product boundary.

**Consequences.** CMS-shaped feature requests are now planned into the office layer instead of declined. The docket graduates from a minimal case list to the primary daily surface. The GUI reorganizes into Court and Office panes. The workspace gains an office-core crate whose schema is written for eventual PostgreSQL portability behind a future evidence-server, while shipping local-first on SQLite. The evidence roadmap (case-assembly milestone, TensorRT intake) continues in parallel and becomes the differentiating feature surfaced inside the office layer, not a subordinate of it. The open distribution question gains urgency: the DefenderData-alternative positioning presumes open source, but distribution.open-source-for-public-defenders remains the record that decides it. Roadmap and boundary detail live in docs/office-layer-plan.md.

**supersedes** `@evidence-intake-project.decision.not-a-case-management-system/1`

## evidence-intake-project.decision.painted-window-chrome

### Revision 1 — The Windows frontend keeps native buttons and paints its own depth and grouping

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.painted-window-chrome/1` · scope `path "src/gui/winsafe.rs"`

The WinSafe frontend keeps stock Win32 push buttons and adds depth and grouping by painting the parent window in WM_PAINT, rather than by owner-drawing the buttons. Each button gets a two-band drop shadow offset down and right -- #EC then #DE against the #F0F0F0 BTNFACE background, the darker band painted last so it lands against the button's own edge -- and etched rules separate the rail's three command groups and the review panel from the output above it. Owner-draw was rejected because it would have to reimplement hover, focus, pressed, disabled, and high-contrast rendering, and would then drift from whatever the user's Windows theme does; painting only the space around a button buys the depth without owning any of the button's state.

## evidence-intake-project.decision.single-broker-inference

### Revision 1 — All live GPU inference uses the Evidence TensorRT broker

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.single-broker-inference/1` · scope `path "adapters/**"`, `path "runtime/**"`, `path "scripts/**"`, `path "src/gui/**"`

Document OCR, video clock OCR, visual embeddings, object detection, audio transcription and scene captioning use one versioned fail-closed Evidence TensorRT broker. Adapters may retain JSON fixture backends for tests, but no live adapter owns a second GPU runtime, downloads models, silently falls back, or asks an operator to type an unverified model revision.

**Context.** The document, audio and video adapters already share the NormalizedBatch contract, while live GPU implementations had diverged across an in-process Whisper engine, a Lege-owned TurboOCR worker and ad hoc video CLIs.

**Consequences.** The GUI discovers installed model identities from the broker; Lege keeps PDF/DocIR ownership through a broker bridge; model packs and workers are checksummed, revision-pinned and supervised once.

**supersedes** `@evidence-intake-project.decision.audio-adapter-native-whisper-engine/1`

## evidence-intake-project.decision.structure-not-verdict

### Revision 1 — Decision views report structure; they never score, rank, or predict a case

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.structure-not-verdict/1` · scope `path "docs/domain-rules.md"`, `path "docs/search.md"`, `path "docs/standing.md"`, `path "src/store.rs"`, `path "src/views.rs"` · topic `presentation`

Read models may report facts about how a case's material is connected -- distinct originals behind an element, a sole source carrying it, unchecked support, whether a gap touches a charge -- and may order results by such facts. They may not score a charge, rank elements by strength, label anything weak, or estimate an outcome. Full-text relevance ranking is permitted because it ranks text matches rather than evidence, and the relevance value is not reported. The product goal is a defender understanding what they have in minutes, which needs more than an inventory; the risk is that a strength number is a rearrangement of counts they could already see, carrying an authority it has not earned, and a defender reading one stops looking. Reporting structure gives the same speed while every claim stays checkable and arguable.

## evidence-intake-project.decision.three-intake-modalities-locked

### Revision 2 — Keep document, audio and video as the complete intake modality set

`active` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.three-intake-modalities-locked/2` · scope `all`

The product's intake modalities are document, audio and video. Further work improves their adapters, shared provenance, review, search and collation rather than adding another evidence modality. A future map may only be a presentation of location anchors already supplied or reviewed; 3D scene mapping, photogrammetry, trajectory reconstruction and other forensic reconstruction are outside this product scope.

**Context.** The three pipelines now cover the intended discovery media. The owner explicitly locked the feature set after reviewing speculative 3D mapping and ordinary digital-map ideas.

**Consequences.** Integration and reviewer workflow take priority over new modality experiments. Mapping is eligible only as a provenance-preserving collation view that returns the reviewer to the underlying source and does not infer a scene, route, measurement or common event.

**supersedes** `@evidence-intake-project.decision.three-intake-modalities-locked/1`

## evidence-intake-project.decision.video-intake-points-never-asserts

### Revision 1 — Video is in scope as intake that points at the original; video analysis that asserts a fact is forensics and out

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.decision.video-intake-points-never-asserts/1` · scope `path "adapters/audio/**"`, `path "adapters/video/**"`, `path "src/export.rs"`, `path "src/suggest.rs"`

The video adapter stays in the product, and the line it may not cross is not "video versus no video" but "point versus assert". Every output of video intake is a locator on the original -- container hash, start and end time on the original timeline, and a derived still -- carrying a suggested, machine-stamped label that tells a lawyer where to look. No video output ever states what the video shows as a fact: it never names a person, never verifies itself, never reaches an export as anything but an unreviewed machine suggestion. Reviewing discovery, including watching every minute of body-worn camera, is core defense work; producing a new evidentiary claim from footage that an expert would have to sponsor is forensics and belongs to a retained expert, not this software.

In scope, in priority order. Tier 1, deterministic and no neural net: container hash and metadata (device, claimed versus actual duration, creation time), scene cuts, dropout and recording_gap, silent-segment detection, OCR of the burned-in clock overlay as raw_time per scene, multi-camera alignment by audio cross-correlation, and the video's audio track through the audio adapter (ASR with anonymous SPEAKER_nn diarization). Tier 2, a coarse visual finder that runs overnight and is optional: per-keyframe text-to-frame retrieval (CLIP/SigLIP-class embeddings, or open-vocabulary boxes from OWLv2/Grounding-DINO/YOLO-World-class detectors) tuned for recall over precision because a person reviews every hit; and one VLM caption per scene as a skim index, indexed by FTS as machine-generated content of a derived source. Tier 3 is excluded by @evidence-intake-project.video.no-forensic-assertions.

**Context.** Body-worn camera is the dominant discovery burden, not a corner case: an OJP survey found BWC review takes more than ten hours a month for over two-thirds of defenders and 63% say most cases carry audiovisual evidence; felony attorneys in some offices carry about 100 cases with four to six hours of BWC each and review by watching and typing into Word; 93% of Virginia defenders reported being unable to review all footage. Practitioner threads in r/publicdefenders show Axon links stored in the case-management system as routine. So dropping video would leave out the modality that costs the most hours -- but those hours are spent finding things in footage, not analysing it, which is what fixes the boundary. The closed-set detectors (COCO has no gun class) and the vendored gun-detection paper are finders for one class each; embedding retrieval indexes once and answers arbitrary queries later, which suits a tool that cannot predict what a defense will need. Identity claims (face, gait, voice, speaker-to-face) are the exact thing rules 1 and 3 and the no-automatic-possibly_same_person invariant already forbid a machine to make. Speed, enhancement, authenticity and reconstruction each produce an assertion needing calibration or an expert.

**Consequences.** The four proposed video work records (scene-core, detector-observations, scene-captions, analyze-job) implement this decision and keep their cannot-verify claims. Detections and captions may be searched and reviewed but never quoted in an export as fact; the export read models treat them as unreviewed inclusions and count them in the header. Video adds two deterministic slices before any further model work: clock-overlay OCR (@evidence-intake-project.video.clock-overlay-ocr) and cross-camera audio sync (@evidence-intake-project.video.audio-cross-correlation-sync), and routes its audio through the audio adapter (@evidence-intake-project.video.audio-track-through-audio-adapter). Text-to-frame retrieval (@evidence-intake-project.video.keyframe-embedding-retrieval) is the preferred visual finder over adding detector classes. The GUI must render machine video suggestions as visibly unreviewed and one action from the original still and time range, since the remaining risk is social: a caption that reads like a finding.
